gloss: to have no prospect; have nothing to go on

definitions.gloss: to have no prospect; have nothing to go on; have no clue
definitions.explanation: Indicates a lack of any reliable lead, plan, or person to depend on for achieving something. {当|あ}て means a dependable hope or expectation.

examples.japanese: {就職|しゅうしょく}の{当|あ}てがない。
{泊|と}まる{当|あ}てがないまま{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I set off on the trip with no place to stay lined up.

examples.japanese: お{金|かね}を{借|か}りる{当|あ}てがなくて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: I'm in trouble because I have no one to borrow money from.

notes:
{当|あ}て means a dependable hope or expectation — a person, plan, or resource one can rely on. The negative ～がない states that no such thing exists.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {就職|しゅうしょく}の{当|あ}てがない: to have no job prospects
- {当|あ}てもなく{歩|ある}く: to walk with no destination in mind
- {当|あ}てがはずれる: one's expectations are disappointed

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見込|みこ}みがない: to have no prospects — emphasizes the likelihood of success
- {当|あ}てにする: to count on — the positive expression, 'to rely on something'
